desc:
A data structure keeps a growing set of numbers split into two halves: the lower half (the smaller numbers) and the upper half (the larger ones). Each half is given as an array in arbitrary order.

The split is valid when all three conditions hold:

  • lower is not empty;
  • lower has the same number of elements as upper, or exactly one more;
  • every value of lower is less than or equal to every value of upper (equal values on both sides are fine).

If the split is valid, return a one-element array holding twice the median of all the numbers (the median of an even count is the average of the two middle values, so doubling keeps everything an integer). If the split is not valid, return an empty array.

lower = [3, 1, 2], upper = [5, 4, 9]   -> [7]   (middle values 3 and 4)
lower = [4, 1, 3], upper = [7, 5]      -> [8]   (median 4, doubled)
lower = [2, 9],    upper = [5]         -> []    (9 is larger than 5)
constraints: The arrays are not sorted and may contain duplicates
hints: Check the sizes first: lower must be non-empty and its size may exceed the size of upper by 0 or 1 only.
You do not need to compare every pair. The order condition holds exactly when the largest value of lower is at most the smallest value of upper.
If valid: with an odd total the median is max(lower) (answer twice that); with an even total it is the mean of max(lower) and min(upper) (answer their sum).
editorial: This is exactly the invariant a two-heap median structure maintains, written as a checker. The roots of the two heaps are max(lower) and min(upper), so the whole ordering requirement collapses to one comparison between those two values, and the median can be read from them.

Sizes: if lower is larger by one, the total is odd and the median is the extra middle element, max(lower). If the sizes are equal, the total is even and the two middle values are max(lower) and min(upper); their sum is twice the median.
One pass over each array finds the maximum and the minimum, so the time is O(n) with O(1) extra space. Sorting everything would also work but costs O(n log n) and does not check the split.
